newsitem.title: MEXICO: Election propaganda at Mexico university press.
newsitem.headline: Election propaganda at Mexico university press.

text.p: A Mexican university press was found printing leaflets critical of an opposition candidate for a state governorship race just two days before elections are to be held, local media reported on Friday.

The leaflets bore a clear allusion to Fernando Clariond, candidate for governor of Nuevo Leon state, which borders Texas, on the conservative National Action Party (PAN) ticket. They were discovered in the printing press at the Journalism Faculty of the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon state (UANL) in the northern industrial city of Monterrey.

The university, funded by the state, is required to be neutral in Sunday's election. Faculty president Jesus Guerra is spokesman for the State Electoral Commission in Nuevo Leon, the body entrusted with running the election in the state.
"The Honour and Justice Commission will call anyone who might be responsible," University rector Reyes Tamez told local television after he flew from Mexico City to review the matter.

Local PAN activists accused the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) of being responsible for printing the leaflets. "This shows how desperate the PRI are," PAN spokeswoman Sandra Pamanes told Reuters. "We found boxes and boxes of leaflets against the PAN and others in favour of a PRI candidate in a local mayoral race."
PRI officials said they also favoured an investigation but hinted the PAN may have staged the affair to gain electoral advantage.

Nuevo Leon is one of six Mexican states that will elect a governor on Sunday. Mexico will also elect a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City.
The PAN has in recent years wrested control of four out of 31 states in Mexico from PRI, which until 1989 had enjoyed a monopoly of state governors since its foundation in 1929.
